ai.title: Overage rate now plan-aware
ai.summary: Overage billing uses plan-specific rates via new OVERAGE_RATE_PRO ($0.99) and OVERAGE_RATE_PRO_PLUS ($0.90) constants in common/src/constants.ts. Previously the usage page hardcoded $0.90 for all plans, undercharging Pro users. Scope: pricing page and usage page now import these constants; overage calculation drops Math.ceil in favor of exact per-credit rate.

eli5.text: If you’re a Pro subscriber, you were previously being charged $0.90 for each block of 100 extra credits once you went over your monthly limit, even though the pricing page advertised $0.99. Now the system checks which plan you’re on and charges the correct rate, $0.99 for Pro and $0.90 for Pro Plus, so Pro users will see their overage fees match what was promised on the pricing page. You’d notice the difference on your next bill or invoice if you exceeded your quota this month, since the corrected rate applies to the charges you accumulate going forward.

ai.title: Fetch overage rate from Stripe
ai.summary: Overage rate calculation in the usage page now fetches real-time data from Stripe instead of guessing based on total quota. The `UsageData` schema adds an `overageRate` field, and `npm-app` CLI warnings remove hardcoded rates. This ensures users see accurate pricing derived from their active subscription's metered price tiers.

eli5.text: When you go to the usage page, the overage rate shown is now pulled directly from your actual Stripe subscription instead of being guessed from your total quota. The overage rate field was added to the usage data schema, and the CLI warning no longer hardcodes a specific rate. If you look at the usage page, you will see a rate that matches your active subscription's metered price tiers rather than a hardcoded estimate. This change is live today and applies to anyone viewing the usage page with an active subscription.

ai.title: Fix overage rate null handling in usage types and UI
ai.summary: Updated `overageRate` in `usageDataSchema` to `z.number().nullable()` and adjusted local state in `UsagePage` to initialize as `null` instead of `OVERAGE_RATE_PRO`. The web usage page now conditionally renders overage fee details only when `overageRate` is present, preventing errors for users without a defined rate. This ensures correct type safety and UI behavior for accounts lacking an overage rate.

eli5.text: When you go over your monthly credit quota, the usage page now only shows your overage fee details if you actually have an overage rate set for your plan. Previously, some users (like those on free plans) who didn't have an overage rate would see error messages or broken displays; now, the system safely treats the missing rate as 'not applicable' and hides those sections entirely. You would notice that the overage fee breakdown section simply doesn't appear for plans that don't charge overages, instead of seeing a broken or error-filled message.

ai.title: Add codesearch tool using ripgrep
ai.summary: Added code_search tool to system prompt and handlers, enabling pattern search in project files via ripgrep. New handleCodeSearch function in npm-app/src/tool-handlers.ts spawns rg process, truncates output to 10000 chars stdout/1000 chars stderr. Backend main-prompt.ts extracts pattern attribute from code_search calls. Requires @vscode/ripgrep 1.15.9 dependency added to npm-app/package.json and root package.json trustedDependencies.

eli5.text: The assistant can now search through your project's code files to find specific things like function names, variable names, or where something is used, similar to using the search function in a text editor. This works behind the scenes by adding a new capability that leverages a fast file searching tool. For internal users and developers working on the project, this means they can quickly locate code patterns across the entire codebase without manually opening files. This feature is now available in the system.

ai.title: Version 1.0.122
ai.summary: Version bump to 1.0.122. Updates `npm-app/package.json` for the `codebuff` package. Routine release increment.

eli5.text: The software has been updated to version 1.0.122, which bundles several improvements that went live around December 12-17, 2024. If you use the AI assistant, you may notice the documentation website now displays better on both mobile and desktop devices, case study content reads more naturally, and the command you use to stage code changes has become more flexible. Behind the scenes, the tool now supports real-time overage pricing from Stripe, can search through project files using a new code search feature, and handles process controls like Ctrl+Z more reliably. The update also ensures referral credits are applied to invoices before finalization and that signup events are tracked through a new Loops integration.

ai.title: Exclude cta.mdx from Contentlayer build
ai.summary: Added `contentDirExclude` to `web/contentlayer.config.ts` to ignore `case-studies/_cta.mdx` during build. Prevents Contentlayer from processing the partial file as a standalone document. Scope limited to web docs configuration.

eli5.text: Case study pages in the help center will no longer pick up a leftover call-to-action fragment that was never meant to appear on its own. Previously, the system treated the snippet meant only as a reusable part of other pages as if it were a complete page, which could create a broken or unexpected entry in the published documentation. Now the build ignores that fragment, so it never becomes a standalone page that visitors can reach.

ai.title: Fix git stage logic in CLI
ai.summary: Added `changes.length > 0` check to git staging logic in `npm-app/src/cli.ts`. Prevents staging previous changes when no new changes exist. Refactored `staged` variable to `didStage` for clarity.

eli5.text: When you ran a command to save your recent work, the tool would sometimes re-save old work that hadn't actually changed, causing confusion. Now, it checks whether there are any new changes before saving, so it only stages what's actually new. You would notice fewer unnecessary or duplicate save actions when using the staging feature. This fix is already live today.

ai.summary: Version bump to 1.0.123 in `npm-app/package.json`. Internal release increment.

eli5.text: Developers who install this assistant tool will now get version 1.0.123, which includes fixes that stop the setup process from getting confused by leftover draft content and repairs the step that prepares your files to be saved together. If you're a developer running the install command, it'll pull slightly fewer unnecessary files and staging changes that were previously misidentified. The update went live on December 17, 2024.

ai.title: Calculate quota from Stripe metered tiers
ai.summary: QuotaManager adds getStripeSubscriptionQuota to derive limits and overage rates from active Stripe subscription metered price tiers, replacing hardcoded CREDITS_USAGE_LIMITS values. Stripe webhook handleSubscriptionChange and Web usage page now consume this dynamic quota via AuthenticatedQuotaManager, removing redundant direct Stripe API calls from route handlers. Scope covers common/src/billing/quota-manager.ts, web/src/app/api/stripe/webhook/route.ts, and web/src/app/usage/page.tsx. Unhandled webhook events return 405 Method Not Allowed; processing errors return 500 with message instead of silent 405.

eli5.text: When you look at your usage page, your quota and overage rate now come directly from your Stripe subscription's metered pricing tiers instead of being hardcoded values. If you're a paying subscriber, your usage limits and the price per extra unit are now calculated in real-time from your actual Stripe plan, so if your plan changes, your usage page and billing automatically reflect the new limits. Unhandled Stripe webhook events now return a proper error instead of failing silently, and the system reports a 500 error with a message instead of just returning a 405 status.
